==English==
[[Image:Sieve.jpg|thumb|right|Sieve in cooking]]

===Etymology===
From {{inh|en|enm|sive}}, {{m|enm|syfe}}, from {{inh|en|ang|sife}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*sibi||sieve}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*seyp-}}, {{m|ine-pro|*seyb-||to pour, sieve, strain, run, drip}}. Akin to German {{m|de|Sieb}}, Dutch {{m|nl|zeef}}, {{cog|sla-pro|*sito}} (Russian {{m|ru|си́то}}, {{m|ru|сев}}, {{m|ru|се́ять}}).

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/sɪv/}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-sieve.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɪv|s=1}}
* {{homophones|en|civ}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# {{senseid|en|Q381155}}A device with a [[mesh]], [[grate]], or otherwise [[perforated]] bottom to [[separate#Verb|separate]], in a [[granular]] [[material]], larger [[particle]]s from smaller ones, or to separate [[solid]] [[object]]s from a [[liquid]].
#: {{hypo|en|colander|riddle|;|grizzly<id:grate in mining><qq:mining, dialectal>}}
#: {{coordinate terms|en|filter|sile}}
#: {{nearsyn|en|sifter|strainer|temse}}
#: {{ux|en|Use the '''sieve''' to get the pasta from the water.}}
## {{lb|en|obsolete}} A kind of coarse [[basket]].<ref>{{R:Simmonds Trade}}</ref>
# A process, physical or abstract, that arrives at a final result by filtering out unwanted pieces of input from a larger starting set of input.
## {{lb|en|mathematics|number theory}} One of several techniques for counting [[integers]].
##: {{ux|en|Given a list of consecutive numbers starting at 1, the '''Sieve''' of Eratosthenes algorithm will find all of the prime numbers.}}
##* {{quote-web
|en
|year=2010
|author=Luke Mastin
|title=20TH CENTURY MATHEMATICS - ROBINSON AND MATIYASEVICH
|site=www.storyofmathematics.com
|url=http://www.storyofmathematics.com/20th_robinson.html
|accessdate=2013-09-08
|passage=Among, {{sic}} his other achievements, Matiyasevich and his colleague Boris Stechkin also developed an interesting “visual '''sieve'''” for prime numbers, which effectively “crosses out” all the composite numbers, leaving only the primes.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260918223157/https://www.storyofmathematics.com/20th_robinson.html/|archivedate=18 September 2026}}
## {{lb|en|mathematics|category theory}} A collection of [[morphism]]s in a category whose [[codomain]] is a certain fixed [[object]] of that category, which collection is closed under [[precomposition]] by any morphism in the category.
# {{lb|en|colloquial}} A person, or their [[mind]], that cannot [[remember]] things or is unable to keep [[secret]]s.
## {{lb|en|medicine|slang|derogatory}} An [[intern]] who lets too many non-[[serious]] [[case]]s into the [[emergency room]].
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1997|author=Leo Galland|title=The Four Pillars of Healing|page=25
|passage=To be a '''sieve''' was to lack clinical judgment, courage, and group loyalty all at once.}}

==English==

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*peth₂-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|repeten}}, from {{der|en|fro|repeter}}, from {{der|en|la|repetō}}, from the prefix {{m|la|re-||again}} + {{m|la|petō|t=to attack, beseech}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ɹɪˈpiːt/|a=RP}}
** {{audio|en|En-uk-to repeat.ogg|text=to repeat|a=London}}
* {{a|en|GA|CA}}
** {{IPA|en|/ɹəˈpit/|/ɹɪˈpit/|q=verb}}
*** {{audio|en|en-us-repeat.ogg|IPA=/ɹɪˈpit/|a=California}}
*** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Ajshul-repeat.wav|IPA=/ɹəˈpit/|a=CA}}
** {{IPA|en|/ˈɹi.pit/|/ɹəˈpit/|/ɹɪˈpit/|q=noun}}
* {{rhymes|en|iːt|s=2}}

===Verb===
{{wikidata lexeme|L276}}
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To do or say again (and again).
#: {{ux|en|The scientists '''repeated''' the experiment in order to confirm the result.}}
#: {{ux|en|I'll tell you my secret, but first promise me you won't '''repeat''' it to anyone else!}}
#: {{ux|en|I don't mind talking about the incident, but one gets tired of '''repeating''' themself after the hundredth time.}}
#* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=5|passage=When this conversation was '''repeated''' in detail within the hearing of the young woman in question, and undoubtedly for his benefit, Mr. Trevor threw shame to the winds and scandalized the Misses Brewster then and there by proclaiming his father to have been a country storekeeper.}}
#* {{quote-av|en|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=auY3Svvurlk|year=1942|author=w:Franklin Roosevelt|title=Roosevelt Answers Critics - 1942 (1942)|publisher=w:British Pathé|time=1:12
|passage=From Berlin and Tokyo and Rome, we have been described as a nation of weaklings- playboys- who would hire British soldiers or Russian soldiers or Chinese soldiers to do our fighting for us. Let them '''repeat''' that now. Let them tell that to General McArthur and his men. Let them tell that to the sailors who today are hitting hard in the far waters of the Pacific. Let them tell that to the boys in the Flying Fortresses. Let them tell that to the Marines.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|medicine|pharmacy}} To [[refill]] (a [[prescription]]).
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To happen again; [[recur]].
#: {{ux|en|A day like that has not yet '''repeated''' itself.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[echo]] the words of (a person).
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To strike the hours, as a watch does.
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} To make trial of again; to undergo or encounter again.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=a. 1687|author=w:Edmund Waller|title=The Battel of the Summer Islands
|passage=He{{...}} '''repeats''' the danger of the burning town.}}
# {{lb|en|legal|Scotland}} To [[repay]] or [[refund]] (an excess received).
# {{lb|en|procedure word|military}} To call in a previous artillery fire mission with the same ammunition and method either on the coordinates or adjusted either because destruction of the target was insufficient or missed.
#: {{ux|en|Add 100, left 50. '''Repeat''', over.}}
#: {{ux|en|Use "say again" instead of repeat on the radio. '''Repeat''' will bring in artillery fire.}}
# To commit [[fraud]] in an [[election]] by [[vote|voting]] more than once for the same [[candidate]].
